company_description: Boston Scientific Corporation develops, manufactures, and markets medical devices for use in various interventional medical specialties worldwide. The company operates in two segments, MedSurg and Cardiovascular. It offers devices to diagnose and treat a range of gastrointestinal conditions, such as resolution clips, biliary stent systems, stents and electrocautery enhanced delivery systems, SpyGlass, single-use scopes used for diagnostic and therapeutic procedures in the pancreaticobiliary system, in endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography procedures, and single-use duodenoscopes, as well as endoluminal surgery and infection prevention products; devices to treat urological conditions, including ureteral stents, catheters, baskets, guidewires, urinary and bowel dysfunction, sheaths, balloons, single-use digital flexible ureteroscopes, holmium laser systems, penile implants, artificial urinary sphincter, laser system, and hydrogel systems; and devices to treat neurological movement disorders and manage chronic pain, such as spinal cord stimulator systems, radiofrequency ablation, and intraosseous nerve ablation and deep brain stimulation systems. risks.title: Risk of non-compliance with financial covenants
risks.summary: The company must comply with strict leverage ratios tied to its credit facilities (maximum leverage ratio of 4.50x in 2025, reverting to 3.75x). The major financing of the Penumbra acquisition will increase leverage and approach these limits, increasing the risk of non-compliance.
risks.score_rationale: The document explicitly mentions the financial covenants of the 2021 revolving credit facility and leverage ratios. The acquisition of Axonics, closed in November 2024, temporarily increased the allowed ratio to 4.75x. According to the 10-K, as of December 31, 2025, the maximum allowed ratio is 4.50x (reduced from 4.75x) and must reach 3.75x for the remainder of the term. The actual ratio of 1.92x as of December 31, 2025, is currently in compliance, but the announced acquisition of Penumbra for $14.5 billion, financed by $11 billion in debt, will increase leverage. Non-compliance could trigger payment defaults.

risks.title: Risk related to significant acquisitions
risks.summary: BSX's aggressive acquisition strategy, including Axonics (closed), Silk Road Medical, and the announced acquisition of Penumbra for $14.5 billion, increases debt levels and risks related to integration, financing, and shareholder dilution.
risks.score_rationale: The document details the Axonics acquisition closed in November 2024 (a Qualified Acquisition) and the agreement to acquire Penumbra for $14.5 billion (announced in January 2026, Exhibit 2.1). These major transactions, financed through additional debt ($11 billion for Penumbra) and stock, significantly increase consolidated leverage and operational integration risks.

risks.title: Risk of impairment of intangible assets and goodwill
risks.summary: Goodwill and net intangible assets represent 58% of total assets ($25.3B out of $43.7B). An operational slowdown or reduced performance could require a significant impairment, impacting financial results.
risks.score_rationale: The consolidated balance sheet as of December 31, 2025, shows goodwill of $18.282 billion (41.9% of total assets) and net intangible assets of $7.019 billion (16.1% of total assets), totaling $25.301 billion (58.0% of total assets). These high amounts result from past acquisitions (Axonics, Silk Road Medical, Apollo, Relievant, Acotec) and future acquisitions. The fair value estimates used in acquisitions may not materialize, creating a risk of goodwill impairment.
